questions.q: What should the pilot be doing during the flight?
questions.explain: The other tasks belong to the observer and the technician; a distracted pilot is a common cause of accidents.

options: To watch the aircraft and the sky
questions.explain: The observer sees people, birds and other aircraft that the pilot in goggles cannot see.

questions.q: What do you do on loss of link with the aircraft?
options: Report it and watch the failsafe
Rebind the receiver from the radio
questions.explain: The behavior on loss of link is set by the failsafe, which is tested in advance; running around is dangerous.

questions.q: Why must different ELRS radios at a site have different binding phrases?
options: For telemetry to work on the radio
questions.explain: The binding phrase determines the frequency hopping sequence.

questions.q: What is important to know about a crashed aircraft before approaching it?
options: Connect USB right away and download the logs
questions.explain: A damaged LiPo is a fire risk.

questions.q: The main lesson of the case with the occupied E5 channel:
questions.explain: Planning frequencies in advance lets you switch quickly and safely.

questions.q: What is a near miss, and why discuss it?
questions.explain: It is recorded in the debriefing.

questions.q: Who decides “go / no-go” and keeps the logbook?
questions.explain: The pilot is busy only with the aircraft; the decision and the logbook belong to the lead.
